An observability release. Both services now write the same structured logs, expose Prometheus metrics and can send OpenTelemetry traces, so an operator can follow one submission from the request that accepted it through every grading attempt and sandbox call.

Grading is unchanged. So are the definition and outcome formats, the `/api/v1` routes and the GitHub Action: replace `@1.0.0` with `webtech-network/autograder@1.1.0` and nothing else changes. Both services add the unauthenticated `GET /metrics` route and echo an `X-Request-ID` response header. Operators of the HTTP service have two required steps (**migration `012`**, and the sandbox manager command if you override it) and three recommended ones, described below.

## Highlights

- **Structured logs on both services.** The sandbox manager writes the API's log format and reads the same settings: `JSON_LOGS`, `LOG_LEVEL`, `SERVICE_NAME` (default `autograder-sandbox-manager`) and `APP_ENV`. Each request gets one `http_request_completed` line, with the route template as its `path`. `X-Request-ID` is accepted, echoed in the response and forwarded from the API to the sandbox manager. ([log lines](https://github.com/webtech-network/autograder/blob/1.1.0/docs/operate/configuration.md#log-lines))
- **Prometheus metrics** at `GET /metrics` on `autograder-api` (`:8000`) and `autograder-sandbox-manager` (`:8001`): HTTP golden signals, grading throughput, failures and duration, queue backlog, database pool and sandbox pool gauges. Every label has a closed set of values. ([Metrics](https://github.com/webtech-network/autograder/blob/1.1.0/docs/operate/metrics.md))
- **OpenTelemetry tracing**, off unless `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set (OTLP over HTTP; the standard `OTEL_*` variables apply). Traces continue across the API and the sandbox manager, and include AI provider calls and database statements (never their bound values). Each grading attempt is its own trace, linked to the request that accepted the submission. ([traces](https://github.com/webtech-network/autograder/blob/1.1.0/docs/operate/configuration.md#traces))
- **Cleaner logs.** Logs no longer contain sandbox handle IDs, student IDs from paths, client addresses, query strings, AI prompts or provider error messages, even at `DEBUG`.

## Upgrading from 1.0.0 (HTTP service operators)

Follow the [upgrade runbook](https://github.com/webtech-network/autograder/blob/1.1.0/docs/operate/deployment.md#upgrade-runbook) with these steps.

**Required**

1. **Back up the database and run migration `012` with the 1.1.0 image before starting it:** `docker compose run --rm --no-deps api alembic -c web/alembic.ini upgrade head`. The API refuses a database at another revision.
2. **If you override the sandbox manager's command**, start it as the image does: `uvicorn --factory sandbox_manager.api:create_app`. `sandbox_manager.api:app` no longer exists.

**Recommended**

3. **Set the sandbox manager's log environment** in its service definition, like the API's: `JSON_LOGS=true` and your `APP_ENV` (`SERVICE_NAME` defaults to `autograder-sandbox-manager`).
4. **Update log queries that use `request_id`.** `request_id` now means the request that accepted a submission, and all of that submission's attempts share it. To isolate one attempt, use `attempt_id` (API lines) or `trace_id`.
5. **Scrape `/metrics`** from the private network and set `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` to send traces. `/metrics` needs no credential, so your proxy must not forward it.

**Rolling back to 1.0.0:** stop the API and back up the database. Then, while the `api` image is still 1.1.0 (for example `AUTOGRADER_IMAGE_TAG=1.1.0`; the 1.0.0 image does not know revision `012`), run `docker compose run --rm --no-deps api alembic -c web/alembic.ini downgrade 011`. Only then start the 1.0.0 images. The downgrade drops the request ids and trace contexts that 1.1.0 recorded.

- 📋 [Full changelog](https://github.com/webtech-network/autograder/blob/1.1.0/CHANGELOG.md)
